title: The Daily Reconcile

lead.headline: Kubernetes 1.37 lands 67 enhancements, from HPA scale-to-zero to stable KYAML
lead.deck: Sixteen features go stable, 23 move to beta and 27 debut in alpha. These are the ones that change day-to-day work for cluster and platform operators.
text: The release ships 67 enhancements: 16 stable, 23 beta, 27 alpha and one deprecation. The headline stable feature is KYAML, a YAML dialect designed for manifests that removes two long-standing traps: whitespace sensitivity and implicit typing of values.

HorizontalPodAutoscaler scale-to-zero reaches beta and is on by default for workloads scaled on object or external metrics, so idle pods can drop to zero. Manifest-based admission control also moves to beta, Pod-level checkpoint and restore debuts in alpha, and resilient watch cache initialisation is complete, to prevent control-plane outages in large clusters.

On nodes, Memory QoS graduates to beta and needs cgroup v2. Pod-level resource managers reach beta but stay off by default: they read the Pod's .spec.resources, so lightweight sidecars no longer need exclusive cores to get NUMA alignment. Tracking when a PVC was last used goes beta, which helps find forgotten volumes, and new options harden emptyDir permissions and bind mounts.

stories.headline: One control plane for 10,000 accelerators: how China Merchants Bank runs AI on Kubernetes
stories.deck: Training, fine-tuning and inference now share the same hardware, and inference costs fell by more than 60%.
text: The winner of CNCF's end-user case study contest pools nearly 10,000 heterogeneous accelerator cards, 99% of the bank's accelerator resources, under one cloud native framework. Training, fine-tuning and online inference keep separate runtimes but share the hardware.

Each project has one job. Kueue handles admission, queues and quotas, so training jobs cannot reserve capacity before they run. KEDA scales inference on live demand. HAMi splits accelerators into fine-grained units for both paths, Fluid speeds up access to datasets and model weights, and Prometheus covers observability.

Average accelerator utilisation rose from 35% to over 60%, and inference cost per million tokens fell by more than 60%. The bank's Twinkle framework lets five LoRA tenants share one base model, cutting accelerator use by 80% and raising training density fivefold.

stories.headline: Yassir runs access to 15 tools with Crossplane and Backstage
stories.deck: From Terraform files to a platform that reconciles itself.
text: Under Terraform, reviews never checked whether a change made organisational sense, and a single state file queued even unrelated changes. Now there are two CRDs, Member and Team, plus one Crossplane composition per tool: native providers for GCP, GitHub, PagerDuty and Atlas, the HTTP provider for Slack, Jira and Sentry.

Continuous reconciliation strips any access granted by hand. CODEOWNERS is generated from team files, privileged grants are blocked in CI, and Backstage forms open the same pull requests an engineer would. Compositions are tested with crossplane render in CI. The authors' lesson: getting the right approvers mattered more than the tool.

stories.headline: OpenStack 2026.2 “Hibiscus” ships with 28% more changes
stories.deck: The 34th release, out on September 30, is built around AI-era infrastructure.
text: About 600 contributors landed some 11,500 changes, up 21% and 28% on the Gazpacho cycle. Neutron cut the memory footprint of HA router monitoring by more than fifteen times. The cycle's themes are GPU and accelerator support and confidential computing, and the Vulnerability Management Team coordinated dozens of embargoed advisories.
Hibiscus is not a SLURP release. The next one, Indri, is, so operators on Gazpacho (2026.1) can skip Hibiscus and upgrade straight to Indri.

stories.headline: GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and open-weight MiMo-V2.6 land in one week
text: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol (September 29) costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output, a fifth of GPT-6 Astra, and OpenAI says it nearly matches Astra on agentic coding and computer use. It is in the API and ChatGPT's paid tiers.

Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5 (September 28) keeps Sonnet 5 pricing at $2 and $10. Anthropic says it is over 30% faster and up to 30% cheaper per task, with adaptive thinking on by default; it runs on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure.

Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6 (September 21) is the open option: MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face, a one-million-token context, a Pro model with 1.02 trillion parameters (42 billion active) and a 309-billion-parameter Flash. Xiaomi gives no hardware guidance for self-hosting.

briefs.headline: Three Kubernetes CVEs in a week, one hits multi-tenancy
briefs.text: September 23: CVE-2026-2270, write access to StatefulSets and ControllerRevisions allows creating pods in other namespaces; CVE-2026-76654, subPath symlinks on Windows nodes allow NTLM coercion. September 28: CVE-2026-19444, path traversal in kubectl cp on Windows enables arbitrary file writes. Check the advisories for severity and fixed versions.

briefs.headline: Azimuth adds Kubernetes 1.36 and AMD GPUs, drops Ingress NGINX
briefs.text: StackHPC's Q3 report (September 7): Azimuth 2026.7 brings Kubernetes 1.36 and AMD GPU support; 2026.6 replaced the archived Ingress NGINX with Traefik, with some downtime; 2026.8 moves to Ubuntu 24.04, adds single-node control planes and swaps the deprecated Kubernetes dashboard for Headlamp. Five StackHPC customer systems are on the TOP500, including Sunrise (#67) and Dawn (#111).

briefs.headline: Karmada graduates from the CNCF
briefs.text: Karmada extends the Kubernetes API with PropagationPolicy (where workloads run, with rebalancing across regions, zones and clouds) and OverridePolicy (per-cluster configuration). It schedules multi-component AI training jobs; priority scheduling is now beta and on by default. 1,214 contributors from 292 organisations; users include Bloomberg and Alibaba Cloud.

briefs.headline: Kubernetes 1.34 reaches end of life on October 27
briefs.text: Supported branches are 1.37 (1.37.1), 1.36 (1.36.5), 1.35 (1.35.9) and 1.34 (1.34.12). The next patch release is due October 13, with cherry-picks closing on the 9th. End of life: 1.35 on February 28, 2027, 1.36 on June 28, 2027, 1.37 on October 28, 2027.

briefs.headline: Dell CSM: unauthenticated root on Kubernetes nodes
briefs.text: Container Storage Modules before 1.18.0 let an unauthenticated attacker steal storage admin credentials, gain root on nodes and read Secrets cluster-wide. Upgrade to 1.18.0, restrict network access to the Authorization service with NetworkPolicies, and rotate credentials and Secrets. Six CVEs, from 2026-63688 to 2026-67273.

briefs.headline: Crossplane 2.4.2: security bumps and a ServiceAccount fix
briefs.text: The September 22 patch fixes ServiceAccount ownership being wrongly transferred to new package revisions, bumps the OpenTelemetry OTLP exporter to 1.45.0 for security, and makes a claim fail closed when it cannot list its XRD. Since 2.4, composition functions can watch required resources they do not compose, and safe-start providers scale to zero. Note: the CLI is only distributed from cli.crossplane.io.

briefs.headline: Argo CD 3.5.2: sync fixes and a Dex update
briefs.text: Restores ignoreApplicationDifferences after normalisation and stops auto-sync from being skipped when newer commits arrive mid-sync. Bumps Dex to 2.45.1 and DOMPurify for CVE-2026-49978. No breaking changes documented. Released August 27 alongside 3.4.8.

briefs.headline: “My config repo is not a database”
briefs.text: Alexis Richardson, who coined the term GitOps, lists seven failure modes of using Git as a database: file names as keys, approving templates but deploying rendered output, no transactions for promotions, invisible blast radius, freezes standing in for safety. He suggests versioning rendered output, as Argo CD's Source Hydrator does, and a configuration database alongside Git; his company sells into that category.

briefs.headline: OpenTelemetry and Prometheus are finally getting along
briefs.text: In the 2026 survey, ease of use rose from 3.1 to 3.6 and the share finding the combination hard fell from 29% to 10%. Nearly 50% mix both for infrastructure metrics. Open gaps: data model, resource attributes and naming. Atlassian moved 100,000 hosts to OpenTelemetry and cut aggregation CPU by about 50% and sidecar cost by 30%.

briefs.headline: Kubeflow and Buildpacks graduate, k8gb incubates
briefs.text: Kubeflow graduated on August 17 and Cloud Native Buildpacks on August 11; k8gb, the Kubernetes global load balancer, became incubating on August 5. The KubeCon NA 2026 schedule adds an AI Inference and Agentic track.

cartoon.caption: Water can wait. First, the password.
cartoon.explanation: An exhausted traveller crosses the desert and finally reaches the oasis. He ignores the pond under the palm tree and crawls towards the free Wi-Fi sign instead. The joke is about how connectivity has become a “basic need”, almost ahead of water.
